instruction: You are a strategic corporate innovation advisor. Analyse the company profile and survey responses, then respond ONLY with a valid JSON object containing maturity_score, opportunities, next_steps, and key_weaknesses.

answers.companyDescription: Mental health tech company offering an app-based cognitive behavioral therapy program with human therapist chat support. Our platform integrates secure telehealth and personalized content modules, serving a growing segment of the accessible mental health market. We are actively exploring partnerships in chronic pain management solutions to broaden our clinical scope.
answers.pastInitiatives: We launched a digital customer onboarding flow last quarter that reduced average onboarding time from 12 days to 5 days. The project was cross-functional involving product, compliance, and customer success teams, proving the efficiency of streamlined UX. Early NPS scores for new customers onboarded through this flow are 22 points higher than the legacy process.
answers.strategicGoals: We are heavily dependent on a single product category and a concentrated customer base—our top 3 clients represent 55% of revenue. This concentration risk is unacceptable for our long-term health. We need to identify and develop new revenue streams, possibly including new product lines for different customer segments or entirely new business models that leverage our existing capabilities.
answers.additionalContext: Atlas Networks is currently facing aggressive competition from both established telehealth giants and emerging AI startups in the mental health space, necessitating continuous innovation to maintain market share.
answers.teamSize: Innovation is decentralized across business units, each with its own innovation lead and dedicated resources, coordinated by a group-level Chief Innovation Officer. The total innovation workforce is approximately 100 people across the organization. A group innovation fund of €5M annually is allocated competitively — business units pitch for funding against clear innovation KPIs including revenue from new products and process efficiency gains.

opportunities.title: Corporate Wellness Product Line Launch
opportunities.rationale: Leveraging existing CBT infrastructure to develop B2B corporate wellness packages offers a low-risk entry into a new customer segment and begins revenue diversification immediately. This builds non-dependent revenue streams without requiring deep changes to the core clinical tech.

first_actions: Develop a Minimum Viable Corporate Wellness module based on existing app features.
Conduct market research via targeted surveys with HR departments in 5 key enterprise accounts.
Pilot sales strategy for corporate partnerships.
milestones: Q2: MVP feature complete and internal review.

opportunities.title: AI-Driven Productivity Platform Integration (Radical Diversification)
opportunities.rationale: Developing an AI productivity tool that integrates with the existing mental wellness app addresses strategic goals by moving into a completely new business model, potentially accessing entirely different customer acquisition channels. This initiative requires high risk but offers significant market diversification away from pure therapy services.

first_actions: Form an internal cross-functional 'AI Sandbox' team (Product, Data Science, Engineering).
Identify 3 non-health adjacent data streams for preliminary AI use cases.
Allocate a small dedicated budget ($50k) to prototype the core API integration.
resources_needed: Cloud computing resources for initial model training.
execution_plan.success_metric: Achieve 1,000 active AI-driven user integrations by end of Year 2
milestones: Q4: Successful prototype and internal feasibility report.
Year 2: Launch V1.0 integrated productivity feature.

next_steps.action: Formalize the corporate wellness product offering and secure initial budget for pilot testing.
Establish a dedicated, small cross-functional team to define requirements for the AI productivity tool pivot.

key_weaknesses: High dependence on top three revenue streams (55% concentration risk).
Slow, committee-based decision-making process hindering agility.
Limited budget (6%) severely restricts scope for large-scale R&D or comprehensive market entry.
Reliance on informal customer feedback which lacks structured data points.
